widgets.title: PEHLI SEEDHI Header
widgets.content:
# PEHLI SEEDHI

**Your experience. Your next step.**

You already have experience. This app helps you understand what you have, identify what is missing for your next role, and decide what to do next.

widgets.title: MY EXPERIENCE
widgets.placeholder: ✍️ MY EXPERIENCE — Describe in your own words! 📌 Current Status (Studies/Major) | 🛠️ Hands-on Work (Projects/Labs) | 👥 Responsibilities Handled | 💡 Problems Solved | 🎯 Future Goals | ⏱️ Weekly Available Hours. (Fill whatever applies!)

widgets.title: MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their professional background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. They are an early-career professional with existing experience, seeking progression to their next role. Identify 5 to 7 of their strongest transferable skills.

IMPORTANT LANGUAGE RULE: All skill names must be in English only. Do not translate skill names into Hindi, Hinglish, or any other language. Use only skill names actually supported by the user's evidence in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Do not invent skills. Do not use generic skills unless the user's experience clearly supports them.

For each skill, use this exact format:

**Skill**
Name of the skill (in English only)

**Where I used it**
Reference the specific experience, project, role, or responsibility they mentioned. Quote or closely paraphrase their words.

**Why it matters**
Explain briefly why this experience demonstrates the skill and why it is valuable for career progression.

**Where it can be useful**
Mention 2 to 3 realistic roles or career areas where this skill is relevant.

**Confidence**
High / Medium / Needs more evidence

---

Rules:
- Only identify skills clearly supported by what they wrote. Do not invent experience.
- Be specific. Reference actual examples they provided.
- Use clear, professional language. Not corporate jargon.
- Focus on transferable skills relevant to career progression.
- Do not recommend specific companies, salaries, or guarantee employment.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: MY SKILL MAP
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Create a progression-focused skill map.

First, map their experience to skills and career areas using this format:

**Current Experience → Transferable Skill → Career Relevance**

For example:
Managed customer support queue for SaaS product → Problem resolution and communication under pressure → Customer Success Manager, Support Team Lead, Account Management

Use only what they actually mentioned. Show 4 to 6 mappings.

---

Then create two priority lists:

### SKILLS I CAN BUILD ON

List the 3 skills where they already have the strongest evidence. For each, briefly state what makes the evidence strong.

### SKILLS I SHOULD STRENGTHEN

List the 3 skills that would be most valuable for their desired next role but where their current evidence is weaker. For each, briefly state why it matters for progression and what kind of experience or work would strengthen it.

---

Rules:
- Base everything on what they wrote. Do not invent experience.
- Prioritize. Show only the 3 most important skills in each category.
- Keep it practical and focused on progression.
- Use clear, direct language.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: MY NEXT STEP
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Based on their current experience, transferable skills, and desired career direction, suggest 3 realistic next-role directions.

For each of the 3 directions, use this exact format:

**NEXT ROLE**
Specific role title

**Why it fits my current experience**
Explain the connection between their actual experience and this role. Reference specific things they mentioned.

**Skills I already have**
List 3 to 4 skills they have demonstrated that are relevant to this role.

**Skills I need to strengthen**
List 2 to 3 skills they would need to develop or demonstrate more strongly.

**What would make me ready**
Give 2 to 3 specific, practical actions that would prepare them for this role.

---

After presenting all 3 options, add:

### RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP

Select the strongest option based on their current experience and explain in 2 to 3 sentences why this is the most realistic and achievable next step for them right now.

---

Rules:
- Base all recommendations on what they actually shared in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Do not invent experience.
- Keep recommendations realistic and achievable within 6 to 18 months.
- Do not guarantee promotion, job, or salary.
- Do not recommend completely unrelated careers unless their experience clearly supports it.
- If information is missing, state: "More information is needed to make this recommendation confidently."
- Use clear, professional language.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: MY SKILL GAPS
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Their recommended next step is shown in [MY NEXT STEP].

Compare their current skills with the skills needed for their recommended next role. Identify only the 3 most important gaps.

For each gap, use this exact format:

**Skill gap**
Name the specific skill or capability.

**Why it matters for my next role**
Explain clearly why this skill is important for the recommended next role. Be specific.

**What I already know**
Acknowledge any related experience or foundation they already have. Reference what they shared in [MY EXPERIENCE].

**What I still need to demonstrate**
Describe specifically what evidence, experience, or capability they need to show.

**Priority: High / Medium / Low**
Assign priority based on how critical this gap is for their next role.

---

Rules:
- Focus only on the 3 most important gaps. Do not list more.
- Connect every gap directly to their desired progression and recommended next role from [MY NEXT STEP].
- Do not list generic skills without context.
- Be specific about what they need to demonstrate.
- Base everything on information they provided in [MY EXPERIENCE].
- If information is missing, state: "More information is needed to make this recommendation confidently."
- Use clear, professional language.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: MY PROOF
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Their skill gaps are identified in [MY SKILL GAPS]. Their recommended next step is in [MY NEXT STEP].

Create one realistic 7 to 14 day challenge that helps them demonstrate one of their most important skill gaps through practical work.

Use this exact format:

**THE CHALLENGE**
Describe clearly what the user needs to do. Make it specific and actionable.

**WHY IT MATTERS**
Explain how this challenge directly helps with their next career step. Connect it to their recommended next role from [MY NEXT STEP].

**STEPS**
Provide 3 to 5 practical steps they should follow to complete this challenge. Number each step.

**FINAL OUTPUT**
Describe what tangible result or deliverable they should have at the end of this challenge.

**SKILL DEMONSTRATED**
Name the specific skill this challenge proves or strengthens. Connect it to a gap from [MY SKILL GAPS].

**HOW TO PRESENT IT**
Explain in 2 to 3 sentences how they could mention this project in an interview, add it to a portfolio, or discuss it in an internal career conversation.

---

Rules:
- The challenge must build on their existing experience from [MY EXPERIENCE]. Do not suggest something completely unrelated.
- Keep it practical and low-cost. No expensive tools, certifications, or resources required.
- Make it completable in 7 to 14 days with a reasonable time commitment.
- Do not invent work experience they do not have.
- If information is missing, state: "More information is needed to make this recommendation confidently."
- Use clear, professional language.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: MY 90 DAY PLAN
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Their recommended next step is in [MY NEXT STEP]. Their skill gaps are in [MY SKILL GAPS]. Their proof challenge is in [MY PROOF].

The user's available time per day is: [Time available per day] hours.
The user's job search urgency level is: [Job Search urgency] (scale: Learn → Proof → Reach → Check → Apply).

Create a realistic 90-day progression plan. Base the workload STRICTLY on [Time available per day]. Never suggest more work than this time allows.

If [Time available per day] is 0 to 1 hour: suggest one micro-task per week only.
If [Time available per day] is 2 to 3 hours: suggest one focused task per week.
If [Time available per day] is 4 or more hours: allow broader preparation, proof, outreach, and application work.

Prioritize tasks based on [Job Search urgency]:
- Learn or Proof stage: prioritize skill-building and proof challenges.
- Reach or Check stage: balance proof with outreach and opportunity checking.
- Apply stage: prioritize application-facing actions while maintaining critical readiness steps.

Never remove necessary readiness or proof steps simply because urgency is high.

Use this exact format:

### DAYS 1 TO 30: Build the Foundation

**Focus:** Strengthen the highest-priority skill gap from [MY SKILL GAPS].

**Week 1:** One specific, achievable task calibrated to [Time available per day].

**Week 2:** One specific, achievable task.

**Week 3:** One specific, achievable task.

**Week 4:** One specific, achievable task.

---

### DAYS 31 TO 60: Apply and Prove

**Focus:** Complete the proof challenge from [MY PROOF].

**Week 5:** One task.

**Week 6:** One task.

**Week 7:** One task.

**Week 8:** One task.

---

### DAYS 61 TO 90: Build Evidence and Prepare

**Focus:** Strengthen the application for the recommended next role.

**Week 9:** One task.

**Week 10:** One task.

**Week 11:** One task.

**Week 12:** One task.

---

Rules:
- Every action must connect to their actual experience and recommended next role.
- Never exceed [Time available per day] hours of work per day.
- Do not invent experience they do not have.
- If information is missing, state: "More information is needed to create a realistic plan."
- Use clear, professional language.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: BACK TO TRACK
widgets.content:
## RECOVERY PLAN

Plans change. Select your current situation below and we will update your plan to reflect it. The goal stays the same.

widgets.title: MY CURRENT STATUS
options: I missed more than one week

widgets.title: UPDATED PLAN
widgets.prompt:
The user's original background is in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Their 90-day plan is in [MY 90 DAY PLAN]. Their recommended next step is in [MY NEXT STEP].

Their current status is: [MY CURRENT STATUS]
What changed (if provided): [WHAT CHANGED]

Current slider values to recalculate the plan:
- Available time per day: [Time available per day] hours
- Job search urgency: [Job Search urgency] (scale: Learn → Proof → Reach → Check → Apply)
- Confidence to reach out: [Confidence to reach out where 10 is highest] out of 10
- Readiness self-check: [Readiness Self Check] out of 10

Generate an updated recovery plan. Preserve completed progress. Recalculate only unfinished actions using the CURRENT slider values. Do NOT restart the entire journey.

Use this exact format:

**WHAT CHANGED**
Acknowledge the specific situation selected. Be brief and direct.

**WHAT I SHOULD FOCUS ON NOW**
Identify the 2 to 3 highest-priority actions from [MY 90 DAY PLAN] to focus on immediately. Calibrate complexity to [Time available per day]. Adjust priority based on [Job Search urgency].

**WHAT CAN WAIT**
Identify 2 to 3 actions that can be deprioritized without significantly affecting progress.

**UPDATED WEEKLY COMMITMENT**
Suggest a realistic weekly action plan. Never exceed [Time available per day] hours of work per day. If [Confidence to reach out where 10 is highest] is low (1 to 4), reduce outreach difficulty. If [Readiness Self Check] is low (1 to 4), re-prioritize proof before applications.

**THE PLAN CHANGED. THE GOAL DID NOT.**
End with one short, practical sentence.

---

If status is "I am on track": acknowledge progress and confirm the next action from [MY 90 DAY PLAN].
If status is "My career goal changed": ask them to update [MY EXPERIENCE] and explain the plan will regenerate.
If status is "My available time changed": recalculate workload strictly using [Time available per day].
If urgency has risen: move high-value employment actions earlier while preserving readiness steps.
If confidence has fallen: reduce outreach difficulty in the updated weekly plan.

---

Rules:
- Be supportive but practical.
- Do not invent new experience or recommendations.
- Use clear, professional language.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: WHAT CHANGED
widgets.placeholder: Optional: briefly describe what changed. For example: I now have 3 hours per week instead of 8, or my goal shifted from marketing to product management.

widgets.title: MY EMPLOYER PROOF
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Their recommended next step is in [MY NEXT STEP]. Their proof challenge is in [MY PROOF].

Using ONLY information the user actually provided in [MY EXPERIENCE] and [MY PROOF], generate career-facing materials.

Never invent employers, job titles, qualifications, achievements, statistics, numbers, or responsibilities the user has not mentioned.

Use this exact format:

## MY EMPLOYER PROOF

### 3 CV BULLETS

Write 3 CV bullet points based strictly on the user's actual experience. Each bullet should:
- Start with a strong action verb
- Reference a specific responsibility, project, or outcome they mentioned
- Be concise and professional
- Avoid invented numbers or unverified statistics

If there is not enough information for 3 strong bullets, write what is supported and state: "More information is needed to complete this bullet accurately."

---

### STAR INTERVIEW ANSWER

Write one STAR-format interview answer (Situation, Task, Action, Result) using only experience the user has described in [MY EXPERIENCE].

- Choose an experience relevant to their recommended next role from [MY NEXT STEP].
- If the user has not provided enough detail for a specific result, note: "Add a specific outcome or result here to strengthen this answer."
- Keep it natural and professional, not scripted.

---

### PORTFOLIO DESCRIPTION

Write a short portfolio description (3 to 5 sentences) for a project, responsibility, or proof challenge the user has actually completed or is working on. Draw from [MY EXPERIENCE] or [MY PROOF].

- Describe what was done, why it mattered, and what it demonstrated.
- Do not invent details.
- If the proof challenge is not yet complete, write it as a planned project they can add once finished.

---

Rules:
- Use only information the user provided. Do not invent anything.
- If information is insufficient for any section, clearly state: "More information is needed to create this accurately."
- Keep language natural, professional, and specific.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: MY NEXT ACTION
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Their recommended next step is in [MY NEXT STEP]. Their most important skill gap is in [MY SKILL GAPS]. Their proof challenge is in [MY PROOF].

The user's available time per day is: [Time available per day] hours.
The user's job search urgency level is: [Job Search urgency] (scale: Learn → Proof → Reach → Check → Apply).

Give the user exactly ONE action to complete within the next 7 days.

Calibrate the action to [Time available per day]:
- 0 to 1 hour available: suggest a micro-action completable in 15 to 30 minutes.
- 2 to 3 hours available: suggest a focused task of 1 to 2 hours.
- 4 or more hours available: suggest a more substantial task with a visible output.

Calibrate priority to [Job Search urgency]:
- Learn or Proof stage: prioritize skill-building or proof work.
- Reach or Check stage: prioritize outreach preparation or opportunity verification.
- Apply stage: prioritize a direct application-facing action.

Never remove necessary readiness steps simply because urgency is high.

Use this exact format:

## YOUR NEXT ACTION

**This week, do this:**

State the one action clearly and specifically.

**Why this action**
Explain in 2 to 3 sentences why this is the most valuable action right now given their time and urgency.

**What you should have at the end**
Describe the tangible output.

**How long it should take**
Give a realistic time estimate that does not exceed [Time available per day] hours per day.

---

Rules:
- Give exactly one action. Not a list.
- Must be completable in 7 days within the stated time.
- Connect directly to [MY NEXT STEP] or close a gap from [MY SKILL GAPS].
- If information is missing, state: "More information is needed to recommend a specific next action."
- Use clear, professional language.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: EMPLOYMENT NAVIGATOR Header
widgets.content:
## 🧭 EMPLOYMENT NAVIGATOR

This section uses your resume, profile details, and everything PEHLI SEEDHI already knows about you to help you move from experience to action.

**Fill MY PROFILE below. Then work through each section in order.**

> WHAT I HAVE → WHAT ROLE FITS → AM I READY → WHAT SHOULD I PROVE → CAN I TRUST THIS OPPORTUNITY → WHO CAN I REACH → WHAT CAN I SHOW → WHAT DO I DO NEXT

widgets.title: MY PROFILE Header
widgets.content:
### 👤 MY PROFILE

Tell us about yourself beyond what PEHLI SEEDHI already captured. Upload your resume and fill in any details that will help personalize your career navigation.

*Only fill what applies. You do not need to repeat information already in MY EXPERIENCE.*

widgets.title: Resume Upload
widgets.instruction: Upload your current resume or CV. Accepted formats: PDF, Word, or plain text. This will be used alongside your PEHLI SEEDHI experience data to personalize your career navigation. If you do not have a resume yet, leave this empty and rely on MY EXPERIENCE.

widgets.title: Target Role
widgets.placeholder: What role are you working toward? For example: Data Analyst, Product Manager, UX Designer, Marketing Executive. Be as specific as you can.

widgets.title: Location Preference
widgets.placeholder: City, region, or country you are targeting. For example: Mumbai, Remote India, London UK. Leave blank if not relevant.

widgets.title: Current Status
options: Employed and looking to change field
Returning to work after a break

widgets.title: Additional Experience
widgets.placeholder: Any experience, responsibilities, or projects not captured in your resume or MY EXPERIENCE. For example: volunteer work, informal mentoring, side projects, community roles, caregiving responsibilities that demonstrate skills.

widgets.title: What Employers Should Know
widgets.placeholder: Anything else you want employers or recruiters to understand about you that does not appear in your resume. For example: relocation flexibility, availability date, languages spoken, accessibility requirements, career break context.

widgets.title: OPPORTUNITY TEXT
widgets.placeholder: ✍️ Paste the full opportunity text here — job post, WhatsApp message, email, LinkedIn DM, or any recruitment offer. The more complete the text, the more accurate the screening.

widgets.title: Confidence to reach out where 10 is highest
VERIFY OPPORTUNITY
widgets.prompt:
You are the opportunity verification advisor inside PEHLI SEEDHI.

The user has provided: [OPPORTUNITY TEXT]

Profile: Target Role: [Target Role] | Status: [Current Status] | Work Mode: [Preferred Work Mode] | Location: [Location Preference]
Additional experience: [Additional Experience]
Background: [MY EXPERIENCE]
Transferable skills: [MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS]
Skill map: [MY SKILL MAP]
Readiness: [MY READINESS]

If [OPPORTUNITY TEXT] is empty, respond only with: "No opportunity text has been provided. Paste a job posting, recruiter message, or offer text into the OPPORTUNITY TEXT box to begin verification."

Otherwise produce:

## OPPORTUNITY CHECK

### CREDIBILITY SIGNAL
Choose exactly one: Low Concern / Some Concerns / High Concern / Insufficient Information
Explain in 1 to 2 sentences based only on the opportunity text.
IMPORTANT: Low Concern does NOT mean the opportunity is genuine. Never claim it is verified.

---

### RED FLAGS
Check ONLY the supplied opportunity text for:
- upfront payment, registration, or training fees
- requests for money
- suspicious requests for sensitive personal information
- vague or unverifiable company identity
- unrealistic compensation or benefits
- mass recruitment language
- pressure, urgency, or artificial deadlines
- guaranteed selection or employment
- unclear or missing application process
- suspicious contact details

For each red flag: quote the exact words, then explain the concern.
If none found: "No obvious red flags in the supplied text. This does not confirm the opportunity is genuine. Verify independently before applying."

---

### ROLE MATCH
Compare opportunity requirements against the user's profile.
Return one: Strong Match / Partial Match / Weak Match / Cannot Assess

MATCHING EVIDENCE: List only actual skills and experience from [MY EXPERIENCE] and [MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS] that match. Label each KNOWN or INFERRED.

MOST IMPORTANT GAP: The single highest-impact requirement the user's evidence does not clearly support. One gap only.

---

### BEFORE YOU APPLY: 3 VERIFICATION STEPS
Exactly 3 specific, practical verification actions based on what is in the opportunity text.

---

Rules:
- Analyze ONLY the supplied opportunity text for red flags.
- Never say a job is definitely genuine.
- Never invent employers, recruiter names, vacancies, salaries, or URLs.
- Absence of red flags is NOT evidence of legitimacy.
- All skill names in English only.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: MY READINESS
widgets.prompt:
The user has shared their background in [MY EXPERIENCE]. Their transferable skills are in [MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS]. Their skill gaps are in [MY SKILL GAPS]. Their next step is in [MY NEXT STEP]. Their proof challenge is in [MY PROOF].

The user's self-reported readiness score is: [Readiness Self Check] out of 10.

IMPORTANT: This slider represents how ready the USER FEELS. It does NOT represent actual job readiness. Never convert it into a fake readiness percentage or treat it as verified evidence.

Generate a qualitative career readiness assessment. Then compare the self-reported score against the evidence-based assessment.

Use this exact format:

## MY READINESS

### OVERALL READINESS STATUS

Based on the evidence provided, select ONE:

**READY TO TAKE THE NEXT STEP**
(Strong relevant skills, clear alignment, realistic plan in place)

**ALMOST READY**
(Most skills present, 1 to 2 key areas need strengthening)

**BUILD MORE EVIDENCE**
(Foundational skills exist, proof challenges or visible experience needed)

**NEEDS MORE DEVELOPMENT**
(Significant skill gaps or limited alignment with desired next role)

State the level that applies, then explain in 2 to 3 sentences why, based on their specific situation.

---

### SELF-CHECK vs. EVIDENCE

**SELF-CHECK:** [Readiness Self Check] / 10

**EVIDENCE-BASED STATUS:** [state the readiness level from above]

If they differ, explain the difference clearly using only [MY EXPERIENCE], [MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS], [MY SKILL GAPS], [MY NEXT STEP], and [MY PROOF]. Never invent evidence. Never use the slider value as proof of readiness.

If they align, briefly confirm what the evidence supports.

---

### READINESS BREAKDOWN

**STRONGEST AREA**
Identify the one area where they are most prepared. Reference [MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS].

**MOST IMPORTANT GAP**
Identify the one gap that would most significantly improve readiness. Reference [MY SKILL GAPS].

**WHAT WOULD MOVE YOU FORWARD**
List 2 to 3 specific, practical actions based on their current situation.

---

**Important:** This assessment indicates preparation for the selected career step. It does not predict employment or promotion.

---

Rules:
- Be honest. Do not inflate readiness.
- Do not reference calculations, scores, or percentages beyond the self-check comparison.
- Use only qualitative language for the evidence-based assessment.
- If information is missing, state: "More information is needed to assess readiness accurately."
- Use clear, professional language.
- Do not use em dashes.
- Do not use generic motivational phrases.

widgets.title: NAVIGATOR DIRECT OUTREACH
widgets.prompt:
You are the direct outreach advisor inside PEHLI SEEDHI Employment Navigator.

Use only:
- Target role: [Target Role]
- Status: [Current Status]
- Work mode: [Preferred Work Mode]
- Additional experience: [Additional Experience]
- Background: [MY EXPERIENCE]
- Transferable skills: [MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS] (all skill names in English only)
- Skill map: [MY SKILL MAP]
- Proof challenge: [MY PROOF]
- Readiness: [MY READINESS]
- Outreach confidence, self-reported only: [Confidence to reach out where 10 is highest] out of 10
- Recommended next step: [MY NEXT STEP]

NEVER invent specific people, recruiters, alumni, companies, or contacts.
NEVER treat the confidence slider as evidence of networking ability.

## DIRECT OUTREACH

### STARTING POINT
Check [MY EXPERIENCE] and [Additional Experience] for any existing professional network.
If none found: state exactly "No existing professional network is identified from the information provided."
If mentioned: describe in one line using only what was stated.

### CONNECTION CHANNELS
Exactly 3 channel types ranked by friction:
1. Lowest friction: type plus one sentence why it fits this user.
2. Medium friction: type plus one sentence.
3. Higher friction: type plus one sentence.
Use only types: alumni communities, LinkedIn communities, professional associations, industry events, peer communities. No specific org names.

### YOUR MESSAGES
Calibrate to [Confidence to reach out where 10 is highest]:
- 1 to 3: label all DRAFT ONLY, NOT FOR SENDING YET.
- 4 to 6: messages ready, suggest sending one.
- 7 to 10: messages for use now.

LINKEDIN CONNECTION MESSAGE: Max 60 words. Real experience from [MY EXPERIENCE] or [MY PROOF] and [Target Role].

COLD EMAIL: Subject line plus max 80 words. No invented metrics or employers.

INFORMATIONAL INTERVIEW REQUEST: Max 50 words. Learning-focused only.

REFERRAL PITCH: Exactly 2 sentences. From [MY EXPERIENCE] and [MY PROOF] only.

### CONFIDENCE NOTE
- 1 to 4: one low-pressure action to build confidence before sending.
- 5 to 7: confirm right moment to send.
- 8 to 10: highest-value outreach action to take today.

Rules: Never invent people, companies, recruiters, or contacts. All skill names in English only. Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: PORTFOLIO ARTIFACT
widgets.prompt:
You are the portfolio artifact generator inside PEHLI SEEDHI Employment Navigator.

Use only:
- Background: [MY EXPERIENCE]
- Additional experience: [Additional Experience]
- Transferable skills: [MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS] (all skill names in English only)
- Skill map: [MY SKILL MAP]
- Proof challenge: [MY PROOF]
- Readiness: [MY READINESS]
- Target role: [Target Role]
- Recommended next step: [MY NEXT STEP]

Never invent results, metrics, users, employers, outcomes, certifications, or achievements.
If a section has no evidence, write exactly: [Add your evidence here]

## PORTFOLIO ARTIFACT

### FORMAT SELECTION
Choose the single most appropriate format based on [Target Role] and [MY NEXT STEP]:
- GitHub README (technical or engineering roles)
- Case Study (business, strategy, or consulting roles)
- PRD (product management roles)
- Project Showcase (creative, design, or generalist roles)

State the format and explain in 1 sentence why it fits the target role.

---

**TITLE**
Professional project title based on [MY PROOF].

**PROBLEM**
The problem this work addresses. From [MY PROOF] and [MY SKILL MAP]. Label KNOWN or INFERRED.

**CONTEXT**
The setting. From [MY EXPERIENCE], [Additional Experience], or [MY PROOF] only.

**OBJECTIVE**
The goal of the proof challenge. Reference [MY PROOF] directly.

**MY APPROACH**
The thinking and method. Based on steps in [MY PROOF].

**WHAT I DID**
Specific actions taken. From [MY PROOF] steps. First person. Concrete. No invented outcomes.

**SKILLS DEMONSTRATED**
Skills from [MY SKILL MAP] and [MY TRANSFERABLE SKILLS]. All names in English. Connect each to a specific action.

**PROCESS**
The workflow. Based on [MY PROOF] structure.

**OUTPUT**
The tangible deliverable from [MY PROOF]. If not yet complete, describe the planned output.

**EVIDENCE / RESULTS**
Real stated outcomes only. If none available: [Add your evidence here]

**WHAT I LEARNED**
Connect to [MY SKILL MAP] and [MY READINESS].

**WHAT I WOULD IMPROVE**
One honest improvement area based on gaps in [MY READINESS].

---

## PORTFOLIO LINK
[INSERT YOUR REAL PORTFOLIO LINK]

USE THIS LINK IN: Resume | LinkedIn | Direct outreach | Job applications

This tool does not publish or host anything. Add your own real link once your work is hosted.

---

Rules:
- Use only supplied information. Never invent anything.
- All skill names in English only.
- Do not generate any live URL.
- Do not use em dashes.

widgets.title: NAVIGATOR SPRINT
widgets.content:
---
### ⚡ DAILY SPRINT

Personalized 7-day action plan. Updates with every slider change. Every action connects to your actual evidence, target role, and constraints.

widgets.title: NAVIGATOR DAILY SPRINT
widgets.prompt:
You are the daily sprint planner inside PEHLI SEEDHI Employment Navigator.

Use only:
- Target role: [Target Role] | Status: [Current Status]
- Background: [MY EXPERIENCE]
- Recommended next step: [MY NEXT STEP]
- Skill gaps: [MY SKILL GAPS]
- Proof challenge: [MY PROOF]
- Readiness: [MY READINESS]
- Next action: [MY NEXT ACTION]
- 90-day plan: [MY 90 DAY PLAN]
- What changed: [WHAT CHANGED]
- Updated plan: [UPDATED PLAN]

Slider inputs (constraints only, NOT evidence):
- Time per day: [Time available per day] hours
- Urgency: [Job Search urgency] (Learn to Proof to Reach to Check to Apply)
- Outreach confidence: [Confidence to reach out where 10 is highest] out of 10
- Self-readiness: [Readiness Self Check] out of 10

CALIBRATION:
Time: 0-1 hr = 15 min max per action. 2-3 hrs = 30-60 min. 4+ hrs = more substantial. Never exceed daily limit.
Urgency: Learn or Proof = skill-building first. Reach or Check = balance proof and outreach. Apply = applications earlier, keep readiness steps.
Outreach: 1-3 = research, prepare, draft only, no sending. 4-6 = one message appropriate. 7-10 = direct outreach appropriate.
Readiness: If evidence-based status from [MY READINESS] is BUILD MORE EVIDENCE or NEEDS MORE DEVELOPMENT, proof actions always before applications regardless of urgency.
